title: Itemized domestic grants compared with the return’s expense total
question: Do domestic organization grants itemized on Schedule I exceed the same filer’s Part IX line 1 total by both $10,000 and 5%?
finding: Of 471 comparable returns, 192 agree exactly and 11 exceed both thresholds for review.
how: Use the latest available Form 990 per EIN and period. Add cash and noncash entries in Schedule I Part II. Compare them with the return’s total functional expense for grants to domestic organizations and governments. Include only returns with itemized entries and an explicit Part IX line 1 value.
limits: Reporting instructions, aggregation, classification, accrual timing, recoveries and later amendments can change the comparison. The difference is a reconciliation question, never a loss estimate. Neither Tides year contains an exactly repeated recipient row. Both returns describe accrual accounting and recipient-level adjustments. The audit says refunds and cancellations reduce grant expense. No published grant-by-grant bridge establishes how much of either difference those adjustments explain. Lower Schedule I totals may reflect recipients below the itemization threshold and are excluded. Schedule I, Part II requires an itemized recipient entry when a domestic organization or government receives more than $5,000 in total grants or assistance from the filer during the tax year. Smaller grants may be absent. Under the IRS instructions, an accrual-basis filer following FASB ASC 958 reports the present value of a grant payable in future years. An amount in the cash-grant column therefore does not establish a transfer date.

rows.name: TIDES CENTER
rows.review: Schedule I lists $5,634,644 under Tides Foundation’s name and Tides Center’s own EIN. Schedule R confirms the same outgoing grant and gives the Foundation’s separate EIN. The audit reports a $15.9 million property transfer when Women Building Up separated. Schedule I describes $15,840,627 for Women Building Up and $15,195,000 for 401 State Street WBU LLC as cash. The documents do not equate either row with the property, so the $18,119,899 difference remains unreconciled.

rows.name: TIDES CENTER
rows.review: Schedule R confirms the $8,837,683 Tides Foundation grant in Schedule I. The audit’s Center column shows $42,122,037 of other grants and awards plus $8,837,683 to related parties. Their sum, $50,959,720, equals all three Part IX grant lines together. The narrower domestic-organization comparison still differs by $5,690,613.
